definition: The IBM Shoebox was a 1961 IBM computer that was able to perform mathematical functions and provide speech recognition.
details: It was capable of recognizing 16 spoken words, including the digits from 0 through 9. It was developed by William C. Dersch in the Advanced Systems Development Division Laboratory at IBM

explainer.lead: The IBM Shoebox was a 1961 IBM computer that performed mathematical functions and recognized speech. It is an early milestone in speech recognition hardware.

tiers.eli5: It was a box that could listen to you say numbers and do the math.
tiers.practitioner: Developed by William C. Dersch at IBM's Advanced Systems Development Division Laboratory; its vocabulary was tiny, so it only worked for a fixed set of spoken words.
tiers.paperLevel: Recognized 16 spoken words, including the digits 0 through 9. No broader performance claims are given.

explainer.example: A user speaks a digit aloud and the Shoebox recognizes it as one of its 16 known words.
